notice: The northern coast around AD 1 for Grind Strat (Sweden, Åland, Finland, Estonia): where the sea stood higher against today's land, 500 m cells, in steps of 8 years from AD 1 to 1219, where the 1219 coast takes over. An estimate: today's land uplift (NKG_RF17vel) bent to fit dated lake isolations (north Uppland), over GEBCO's heights; Kopli's neck is a hand-drawn cut. codes.fromMain: cells the 1219 field has as sea in 1219 are stored as 0 and rebuilt from it (src/sim/coast-date.js completeLead)

sgu.note: SGU's shore model is blocked (resource.sgu.se is not allowed): Sweden's AD 1 shore is the estimate, bent to north Uppland (Hedenström and Risberg), as the 1219 coast was bent to Stockholm.

kopli.about: Kopli (Tallinn): Kakumäe joined the mainland about 2800 cal BP, Kopli about 1000 years later (about 1800 cal BP, AD 150) (Saarse and Vassiljev 2010, text); the paper's Fig. 8 (about 2000 cal BP) still shows Kopli as an island and Fig. 9 (about 1000 cal BP) joined. GEBCO's heights at 450 m cannot show the narrow low neck of the Kopli peninsula, so the island is a HAND-DRAWN CUT: the cells under the line below are sea until the year given and land after it. The line (about 59.4465N from 24.655E to 24.725E, carried on along the same line in both directions until it meets today's sea) is our own: in Fig. 8 the strait lies at about 59.448-59.455N, 24.690-24.697E (our reading of the figure against its latitude and longitude ticks), so the line crosses near its southern mouth, within about 300 m. TO CHECK against a survey or a better map. It stands for an estimate, not a survey.
kopli.source: Saarse, L. and Vassiljev, J. (2010), Holocene shore displacement in the surroundings of Tallinn, North Estonia, Estonian Journal of Earth Sciences 59(3), 207-215, doi:10.3176/earth.2010.3.03
